plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Where must a registered person maintain the books of accounts and other records under Section 35 of the CGST Act, 2017?
options: At the principal place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration
At the registered office of the company anywhere outside India
At the residence of the managing director of the company
At any branch office, regardless of whether it is registered or not
plain.explanation: Section 35(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 mandates that every registered person shall keep and maintain all records at his principal place of business as mentioned in the certificate of registration. If more than one place of business is specified in the certificate, the accounts relating to each place of business shall be kept at such places of business.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: For how many years must a registered person maintain books of accounts and records under Section 35(1) of the CGST Act, 2017?
options: 36 months from the due date of furnishing of annual return
72 months from the due date of furnishing of annual return
60 months from the end of the financial year
84 months from the end of the calendar year
plain.explanation: According to Section 35(1), books of accounts and other records must be retained until the expiry of seventy-two months (6 years) from the due date of furnishing of the annual return for the year pertaining to such accounts and records.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the additional retention period for records in a case where an appeal or revision or proceedings are pending before any appellate authority or court?
options: Until one year after final disposal of such appeal or proceedings
For a period of one year after final disposal of such appeal or proceedings, or until the expiry of the regular 72 months, whichever is later
For a period of two years after final disposal of such appeal
No additional period is required if 72 months have passed
plain.explanation: Proviso to Section 35(1) states that a registered person who is a party to an appeal or revision or any other proceedings before any appellate authority or court or is under investigation for an offence, shall retain the books of accounts pertaining to the subject matter for a period of one year after final disposal of such appeal/proceedings or until the expiry of seventy-two months, whichever is later.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following specific records must a manufacturer maintain under Rule 56 of the CGST Rules, 2017?
options: Monthly balance sheet and cash flow statements only
Monthly production accounts showing quantitative details of raw materials or services used and finished goods produced
Stock details of only imported goods
Details of all employees and their salaries
plain.explanation: Rule 56(1) of the CGST Rules, 2017 requires every registered person to keep books of accounts. Specifically, manufacturers must maintain monthly production accounts showing quantitative details of raw materials or services used in manufacture and finished goods produced.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What records must a stockist, broker, or agent dealing in goods maintain under the GST framework?
options: Only bank statements and invoices
True and complete records of goods received and supplied, along with names and addresses of suppliers and buyers
Only tax invoices issued to final consumers
Annual audit reports
plain.explanation: Under Rule 56(3), every agent, broker, or stockist must maintain true and complete records of the quantity of goods received and supplied by them, along with the particulars of the suppliers and buyers.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In what format must accounts and records be maintained and preserved under the GST provisions?
options: Only in physical paper files bound with hard covers
Exclusively on cloud servers hosted within India
Either electronically or manually, provided that electronic records are backed up and accessible
Exclusively in handwritten ledgers authenticated by a Chartered Accountant
plain.explanation: Section 35(1) read with Rule 56 permits the maintenance of books of accounts and other records in electronic form or manually. If maintained electronically, they must be authenticated by way of digital signature and proper backup mechanisms must be in place.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What responsibility is cast upon a registered person maintaining electronic records if called upon by a proper officer?
options: To courier the entire server to the GST office
To provide the details of passwords, access codes, and files in hard copy or readable format along with a signed certification
To allow the officer to change the encryption keys
To print all records and get them notarized
plain.explanation: Rule 57(2) stipulates that the person maintaining electronic records shall produce, on demand, the relevant files, passwords, access codes and numbers, and hard copies of the records as required by the proper officer.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Who is required to maintain a stock register showing receipts, supplies, losses, and balance of goods under Rule 56(4)?
options: Only government undertakings
Every registered person
Only composition taxpayers
Only persons having turnover exceeding Rs. 100 crores
plain.explanation: Rule 56(4) mandates that every registered person shall keep a true and correct account of stock in respect of goods received and supplied by him, including inventories, receipts, dispatches, wastage, and shortage.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Section 35(2), if a registered person fails to maintain accounts and records as specified, what action can the Commissioner or officer authorized take regarding goods?
options: Impose a penalty of Rs. 10,000 only
Determine the amount of tax payable on goods unaccounted for as if such goods had been supplied by him
Cancel the registration without any show-cause notice
Auction the entire factory immediately
plain.explanation: Section 35(2) provides that where the registered person fails to account for the goods or services in accordance with the provisions, the proper officer shall determine the amount of tax payable on the goods or services that are not accounted for, as if such goods or services had been supplied by such person.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What additional records must a godown or warehouse keeper or owner of a transport agency maintain, even if not registered?
options: Only balance sheets of their business
Records of the consigner, consignee, and other relevant details of goods transported, stored, or delivered
Income tax returns of all clients
Audited financial statements for the past 10 years
plain.explanation: Section 35(2) and Rule 58 mandate that every owner or operator of warehouse or godown or any other place used for storage of goods and every transporter, irrespective of whether he is a registered person or not, shall maintain records of consigner, consignee, and goods stored or transported.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: When must transporters and warehouse operators enroll or register on the GST portal if they are not otherwise registered under GST?
options: Within 30 days of starting operations
They are required to enroll and obtain a unique enrollment number in FORM GST ENR-01
They must obtain a regular GSTIN in all states
Enrollment is completely voluntary with no form requirement
plain.explanation: Rule 58 states that persons engaged in transporting goods or operating warehouses, if not registered under GST, shall maintain records and submit an application in FORM GST ENR-01 on the common portal to obtain a unique enrollment number.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What details regarding Input Tax Credit (ITC) must a registered person maintain in their books of accounts under Rule 56?
options: Only the total ITC claimed in the annual return
Monthly accounts showing input tax credit availed, utilized, and balance
Bank certificates of ITC payment
Only the ITC pertaining to capital goods
plain.explanation: Rule 56(2) requires every registered person to keep books of accounts including records of input tax credit availed, utilized, and the balance of ITC available.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Who is required to get their accounts audited by a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant under Section 35(5) of the CGST Act?
options: Every registered person with turnover exceeding Rs. 2 crores
All registered persons
Section 35(5) requiring mandatory GST audit by a CA/CMA has been omitted, and registered persons now submit an Annual Return along with a self-certified Reconciliation Statement (GSTR-9C)
Only companies registered under the Companies Act, 2013
plain.explanation: Section 35(5) which mandated GST audit by a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant was omitted by the Finance Act, 2021. Registered persons now furnish an annual return in GSTR-9 along with a self-certified reconciliation statement in GSTR-9C under Section 44.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Rule 56(11), if a registered person has multiple places of business, where should the accounts relating to each place be kept?
options: At the head office only
At the respective place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration
Anywhere within the home state
At the office of their principal tax consultant
plain.explanation: Rule 56(11) specifies that books of accounts relating to multiple places of business shall be kept at such respective places of business as mentioned in the certificate of registration.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following records must be maintained regarding tax invoice, debit note, and credit note under Rule 56?
options: Only outward invoices issued
Full details of tax invoices, bills of supply, delivery challans, credit notes, and debit notes issued and received
Only copies of invoices exceeding Rs. 50,000
Invoices received from unregistered persons only
plain.explanation: Rule 56(1) requires maintenance of accounts of all goods and services supplied, including invoices, bills of supply, debit notes, credit notes, and delivery challans issued or received.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: If a registered person destroys or misplaces their electronic records, can they plead defense that the computer crashed?
options: Yes, system crashes exempt the person from maintaining records
No, maintaining backup and ensuring safety and recoverability of electronic records is the statutory responsibility of the registered person
Yes, if reported to the police within 24 hours
Only if the server was located outside India
plain.explanation: Rule 57 mandates that the person maintaining electronic records must produce them on demand and ensure proper backups. Failure to maintain or produce records due to system failure without backup does not absolve the taxpayer from statutory penalties.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the consequence if a registered person fails to maintain books of accounts as required under Section 35?
options: Only a warning letter is issued
General penalty provisions under Section 125 may apply along with tax determination on unaccounted goods under Section 35(2)
Automatic imprisonment for 5 years
Suspension of bank accounts by the RBI
plain.explanation: Failure to maintain books of accounts attracts general penalties under Section 125 of the CGST Act, and the proper officer can also invoke Section 35(2) to determine tax on unaccounted goods/services.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Are the accounts maintained by a registered person open to inspection by GST officers?
options: No, inspection requires a court warrant
Yes, upon authorization by an officer not below the rank of Joint Commissioner
Only during the annual filing period
Only if the taxpayer consents in writing
plain.explanation: Under Section 67 of the CGST Act, proper officers authorized by the Commissioner (not below the rank of Joint Commissioner) can inspect places of business and examine books of accounts and records.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What particulars must be maintained regarding 'advance payments' received or made by a registered person?
options: Advance payments are not required to be recorded in GST books
Full details of advances received, adjustments made against supplies, and advance payments made to suppliers
Only advances received in foreign currency
Only advances exceeding Rs. 10 lakhs
plain.explanation: Rule 56(1) explicitly requires maintaining accounts of advances received and paid, along with adjustments made against invoices, as tax liability on advances for services (and earlier goods) requires proper tracking.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a registered person maintain records at a place other than the principal place of business?
options: No, never
Yes, if an additional place of business is declared in the registration certificate or if approved by the Commissioner for specific accounts
Yes, anywhere in the world without notification
Only if the turnover is below Rs. 40 lakhs
plain.explanation: Records must be kept at the principal place of business and additional place(s) of business mentioned in the registration certificate. If records are maintained at multiple places, they must correspond to those specific registered locations.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What specific records must a works contract service provider maintain under Rule 56?
options: Names and addresses of all sub-contractors, property owners, and details of payment, materials consumed, and invoices raised
Only architectural blueprints
Only municipal corporation approvals
Balance sheet of the building owner
plain.explanation: Rule 56(13) mandates that a works contract supplier shall keep separate accounts for each works contract showing names and addresses of employers, suppliers, sub-contractors, description, value, and quantity of goods or services used.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Is a transporter required to maintain records of goods even if the goods are exempt from GST?
options: No, exempt goods need no documentation
Yes, transporters and warehouse keepers must maintain records of all goods transported or stored, regardless of taxability
Only if the value exceeds Rs. 50,000
Only if requested by the transporter association
plain.explanation: Section 35(2) and Rule 58 apply to transporters and warehouse operators for all goods handled by them, irrespective of whether the goods are taxable or exempt from GST.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the consequence of failing to produce electronic records in readable format when demanded by a proper officer?
options: The officer will print them free of cost
It is treated as non-compliance, inviting penal action for failure to maintain/produce records
The taxpayer gets an automatic 30-day extension
The records are permanently deleted from the portal
plain.explanation: Failure to produce electronic records, access codes, and passwords on demand violates Rule 57 and attracts penalties under the provisions of the CGST Act.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following persons is NOT specifically mentioned under Section 35(1) to maintain books of accounts?
options: A registered person
A custodian of goods who is not a registered person
A clearing and forwarding agent
An unregistered individual buying goods for personal consumption
plain.explanation: Unregistered individuals buying goods for personal consumption are final consumers and do not carry on business; hence, they have no statutory obligation to maintain books of accounts under Section 35.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: If records are maintained in electronic form, who must authenticate them?
options: Any employee of the company
The registered person or an authorized representative using a digital signature
The jurisdictional GST Inspector
A statutory auditor
plain.explanation: Rule 57 requires that electronic records must be authenticated by way of digital signature by the registered person or their authorized representative.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What details regarding outward supplies must be kept in the accounts under Rule 56?
options: Total sales figure for the year only
Invoices, debit notes, credit notes, statements of outward supplies, and tax collected and paid
Only cash sales records
Only B2B export supplies
plain.explanation: Rule 56(2) requires maintaining accounts of goods and services imported or exported, and supplies foothills/outward supplies along with tax charged.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: How should a registered person handle corrections or alterations made in manual books of accounts?
options: Correction fluid must be used to erase the wrong entry
Incorrect entry should be scored out under signature, and the correct entry recorded, preserving audit trail
Pages containing errors should be torn out
No corrections are allowed under any circumstances
plain.explanation: Rule 56(5) mandates that manual accounts, registers, and documents shall be maintained sequentially, and any entry shall not be erased, obliterated, or scraped. Corrections should be made properly with initials.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Rule 56, what records must be maintained by an owner or operator of a hotel regarding accommodation?
options: Names and addresses of guests, arrival and departure dates, and room tariff charged
Only food and beverage sales
Only electricity consumption bills
Only employee attendance registers
plain.explanation: Rule 56(7) requires owners or operators of hotels, inns, guest houses, clubs, or similar places to maintain accounts containing details of guests staying, including names and addresses, duration of stay, and room tariff.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the prescribed retention period for accounts and records if an assessment year is under scrutiny for fraud, suppression, or wilful misstatement?
options: 72 months from the due date of annual return
Up to 72 months, but extended if proceedings/appeals are pending or investigation for an offence is active
10 years from the end of the calendar year
Permanent retention
plain.explanation: Under the proviso to Section 35(1), when proceedings/appeals or investigations for an offence are active, records must be retained for one year after final disposal or 72 months, whichever is later.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which authority has the power to notify a class of taxable persons to maintain additional records under Section 35(1)?
options: The State GST Commissioner alone
The Government on the recommendations of the GST Council
The jurisdictional Superintendent of Central Tax
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
plain.explanation: Section 35(1) empowers the Government, on the recommendations of the GST Council, to notify a class of taxable persons to maintain any additional records or accounts as specified.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s Apex Traders, a registered taxpayer under GST in Mumbai, deals in electronic appliances. They have a principal place of business in Andheri and an additional warehouse in Bhiwandi. Due to expansion, they switch from manual ledgers to an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software for maintaining electronic records. The due date for furnishing the annual return for FY 2023-24 was 31st December 2024.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Until what date must M/s Apex Traders mandatorily retain their books of accounts and records for FY 2023-24 under Section 35(1)?
options: 31st December 2029
31st December 2030
31st March 2030
31st December 2031
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 35(1) requires records to be retained for 72 months (6 years) from the due date of furnishing the annual return. Since the due date is 31st December 2024, 72 months expire on 31st December 2030.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Where must M/s Apex Traders keep the accounts pertaining to their Bhiwandi warehouse?
options: Exclusively at their corporate head office in Delhi
At the Bhiwandi warehouse if specified as an additional place of business in the registration certificate
At the residence of the accountant in Mumbai
Anywhere in the State of Maharashtra without registration declaration
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 35(1) and Rule 56(11), accounts relating to each place of business must be kept at such respective place of business mentioned in the certificate of registration.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Since M/s Apex Traders maintain electronic records on ERP software, what is their statutory obligation when demanded by a proper officer?
options: To allow the officer to delete unwanted files
To produce the relevant files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies as required
To provide physical handwritten copies of all ERP entries
To purchase a new server for the GST department
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 57(2) stipulates that the person maintaining electronic records shall produce passwords, access codes, and files on demand by the proper officer.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Suppose an investigation for an offence under GST is initiated against M/s Apex Traders for FY 2023-24, and proceedings are pending on 31st December 2030. When does their record retention obligation end?
options: 31st December 2030 itself
One year after the final disposal of such proceedings or 31st December 2030, whichever is later
Immediately upon the start of investigation
After 10 years from the financial year end
linkedMcqs.explanation: Proviso to Section 35(1) dictates that if proceedings or investigations are pending, records must be retained for one year after final disposal of such proceedings or until the expiry of 72 months, whichever is later.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: Shreeji Transport Agency operates a fleet of trucks transporting goods across multiple states, but is not registered as a taxable supplier under GST. They store goods temporarily in transit godowns located in Gujarat. The proper officer during a verification drive requests Shreeji Transport Agency to produce records of consignments handled during the past quarter.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Shreeji Transport Agency legally required to maintain records of goods despite not being a registered taxable person?
options: No, only registered persons under Section 22/24 must maintain records
Yes, under Section 35(2) and Rule 58, transporters and godown owners must maintain records of consigner, consignee, and goods
Only if their annual turnover exceeds Rs. 20 crores
Only if they cross state borders
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 35(2) and Rule 58 mandate that transporters, warehouse keepers, and godown owners must maintain records of goods transported, stored, or delivered, irrespective of whether they are registered taxpayers.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What registration/enrollment requirement applies to Shreeji Transport Agency on the GST portal if they are not registered under GST?
options: They must obtain a regular GSTIN in Gujarat
They must enroll and obtain a unique enrollment number in FORM GST ENR-01
They must register under the Shops and Establishment Act only
No portal interaction is required
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 58 specifies that transporters not registered under GST shall submit an application in FORM GST ENR-01 on the common portal to obtain a unique enrollment number.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What specific details must Shreeji Transport Agency maintain in their transport records?
options: Only vehicle maintenance bills and diesel receipts
Full details of goods transported, including consigner, consignee, delivery status, and vehicle numbers
Income tax PAN of all drivers
Balance sheet of the transport owner
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Rule 58, transporters must maintain records of goods transported, delivered, or stored in transit, including particulars of consigner and consignee.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Shreeji Transport Agency fails to maintain records as required under Section 35(2), what is the implication?
options: They are immune since they are uninvited transporters
They may face penalties and liability under GST provisions applicable to non-maintenance of records
Their trucks will be gifted to the government
They only receive a verbal warning from the inspector
linkedMcqs.explanation: Failure by transporters or godown keepers to maintain prescribed records attracts penal consequences under the CGST Act provisions.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s BuildWell Engineers, a registered works contractor in Karnataka, undertakes construction of commercial complexes. They engage multiple sub-contractors for electrical, plumbing, and structural works. During an audit by tax authorities, the proper officer asks for contract-wise accounts and details of materials supplied and consumed at various project sites.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under Rule 56(13), what specific accounting obligation is placed on M/s BuildWell Engineers as a works contractor?
options: To maintain a single consolidated bank account statement
To keep separate accounts for each works contract showing names/addresses of employers, suppliers, sub-contractors, and materials used
To audit only the profit and loss account of the head office
To maintain records only for completed contracts
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 56(13) mandates that a works contractor shall keep separate accounts for each works contract showing details of employers, sub-contractors, and quantities/values of goods or services used.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Must M/s BuildWell Engineers maintain records of goods received from sub-contractors at project sites?
options: No, sub-contractors maintain their own records
Yes, true and correct records of goods received and supplied, including wastage and shortage at each site, must be maintained
Only if the value exceeds Rs. 1 crore per site
Only if requested by the local municipality
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 56 requires every registered person, including contractors, to maintain stock accounts and records of inputs received, issued, and stock balances at each operational site.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If M/s BuildWell Engineers fail to account for certain construction materials found at a project site during inspection, how can the proper officer proceed under Section 35(2)?
options: Ignore the discrepancy if total turnover is high
Determine the amount of tax payable on such unaccounted goods as if supplied by them
Order immediate demolition of the building
Suspend the GST registration of the project land owner
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 35(2) empowers the proper officer to determine tax on unaccounted goods or services as if they had been supplied by the registered person.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Where should M/s BuildWell Engineers maintain the site-specific accounts for an ongoing project located in Mysore, given their principal place of business is in Bengaluru?
options: Only at the Bengaluru head office
At the respective project site in Mysore if registered as an additional place of business, or at the principal place of business
At the residence of the site engineer
At the bank locker in Mysore
linkedMcqs.explanation: Accounts relating to each place of business (including project sites registered as additional places of business) must be kept at such places as mentioned in the registration certificate.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. operates a luxury hotel and resort in Udaipur, Rajasthan. The hotel provides accommodation, restaurant services, and banqueting facilities. They maintain their guest registers and billing records electronically through a specialized hotel management software, authenticated by digital signature.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What specific records must M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. maintain under Rule 56(7) regarding hotel operations?
options: Names and addresses of guests, arrival/departure dates, and room tariff charged
Only kitchen grocery purchase bills
Only employee salary and tip registers
Only utility consumption bills
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 56(7) requires owners or operators of hotels and inns to maintain accounts containing details of guests staying, including names and addresses, duration of stay, and room tariffs.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Since M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. uses electronic hotel management software, what must they ensure regarding authentication of records under Rule 57?
options: Records must be printed on paper and signed by hand daily
Electronic records must be authenticated by way of digital signature
Records must be uploaded to the Prime Minister's portal
No authentication is required for software data
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 57 mandates that electronic records maintained by a registered person must be authenticated by way of digital signature.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If a tax officer inspects the hotel and demands the electronic guest logs and access codes, what is the hotel's legal duty?
options: To refuse access citing guest privacy
To produce the relevant files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies on demand
To ask the officer to return with a court order
To encrypt the data permanently
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 57(2) requires the person maintaining electronic records to produce files, passwords, access codes, and hard copies on demand by the proper officer.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: For how long must M/s GreenLeaf Hospitality Ltd. preserve their hotel guest ledgers and restaurant tax invoices for FY 2024-25, assuming the annual return due date is 31st December 2025?
options: Until 31st December 2028
Until 31st December 2031
Permanent preservation
Until 31st March 2028
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 35(1), records must be retained for 72 months from the due date of filing the annual return. 31st December 2025 plus 72 months (6 years) equals 31st December 2031.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s Zenith Distributors is a partnership firm acting as a clearing and forwarding (C&F) agent for various manufacturers in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. They receive goods from principals, store them in godowns, and dispatch them to buyers based on delivery orders. They maintain manual stock registers and issue delivery challans for movement of goods.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What specific records must M/s Zenith Distributors maintain as an agent/stockist under Rule 56(3)?
options: Only income tax returns of principals
True and complete records of goods received and supplied on behalf of every principal, including particulars of principals and buyers
Only bank reconciliation statements
Only transport lorry receipts
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 56(3) mandates that every agent, broker, or stockist must maintain true and complete records of the quantity of goods received and supplied on behalf of every principal.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: How should M/s Zenith Distributors handle corrections or rectifications in their manual stock registers under Rule 56(5)?
options: Use correction fluid or erase entries completely
Ensure entries are not erased or overwritten; any correction must be authenticated under signature preserving the audit trail
Tear out pages containing errors and rewrite the register
No corrections are ever permitted under GST
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 56(5) specifies that manual accounts and registers shall not be erased, obliterated, or scraped, and corrections must be made properly with initials/signatures.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If M/s Zenith Distributors store goods in a separate godown in Tiruvallur, where must the accounts of goods stored in that godown be kept?
options: At the principal place of business in Chennai only
At the Tiruvallur godown if declared as an additional place of business
At the residence of the managing partner
Anywhere outside Tamil Nadu
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 56(11) requires that books of accounts relating to each place of business (including additional places like godowns) shall be kept at such respective place of business mentioned in the registration certificate.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What action can the proper officer take if M/s Zenith Distributors fail to account for goods received from a principal during a stock audit?
options: Levy a flat fine of Rs. 1,000
Determine tax payable on the unaccounted goods as if supplied by M/s Zenith Distributors
Transfer the agency license to another firm
Imprison the partners without trial
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 35(2) provides that if a registered person fails to account for goods or services, the proper officer shall determine the tax payable on such unaccounted goods as if supplied by the registered person.
